context:
Supporter: Hi there, how are you doing?
Seeker: IM HANGING IN THERE HOW ARE YOU?
Supporter: I am okay. What would you like to talk to me about?
Seeker: Well, i have a problem with drinking alcohol I am so scared my job will find out
Supporter: Do you drink when you are at work?
Seeker: I have started calling in atleast twice as week. I have started drinking at work close to the end of my shift in the bathroom
Supporter: That does sound like it might be a big problem. How are your employers reacting? It sounds like you have a big problem that needs professional help, would you agree?
Seeker: They have not mentioned anything to me yet.
Supporter: I think it is likely to have been noticed though, at least.
Seeker: Yes I agree it sounds like a really big problem, but what should i do?
Supporter: I think the best thing would be to be really honest with your employers and ask if you can have time off for professional help.
Seeker: That is a good idea
Supporter: Are you employers likely to be sympathetic?
Seeker: my main concern, that makes me fearful is being fired, and being the talk of the workplace
Supporter: Ah people do love to idly gossip don't they? I've been through that myself. I know it's hard to ignore them but it's best to try.
Seeker: My employer is an well known organization that employees over 3,000 people.
Supporter: I do not know if they can fire you if you have a legitimate medical problem though. Well you could always shame them if they unfairly fired you.
Seeker: Very good to know that I will look into it. It did not start overnight and I don't expect it to end overnight lol, yes that is true. Thank you so much for your time.
Supporter: Large corporations are always over concerned about their images. (we have to talk for fifteen minutes :))
Seeker: oh ok I thought it was just for 10 lines, lol but none the less, there are people really going through that scenario I just portrayex
Supporter: naw there's a time thing too :). Anyway, what sort of therapy do you think would be appropriate for you? To be honest, and I mean this sincerely, I've been through it :(
Seeker: I believe rehabilitative therapy would be best
Supporter: It can be very expensive though. In my country you can get it for free but there's a long waiting list.
Seeker: I have hads a few drinks often but never abused it. thankfully. Well here you might can get help for free, but it does have to be paid back
Supporter: Heh be grateful :) Are you in the US? Our healthcare system is a little less rigid here I think (UK)
Seeker: Yes Im in the United States (Alabama) I heard of the UK so many times but truthfully I know nothing about it
Supporter: Ah you are a long way away from me. I hope that you do manage to sort out your problems though and definitely do talk to your employers Ah it's quite nice here. We pay for healthcare out of our taxes so it's free at source.
Seeker: I will eventually get the courage to, I know how people talk around here, especially in the South\
Supporter: Gossipy people are the worst. Just remind yourself that they all have skeletons in their closets too
Seeker: great advice
Supporter: Well anyway, I hope I have been able to offer your some useful advice. I wish you all of the very best in the future.
Seeker: I think also the best thing to do is to talk to great people like you

Seeker: hi
Supporter: Hello!
Seeker: I'm dealing with a lot of frustration and anxiety.
Supporter: How are you?
Seeker: Frustrated and anxious
Supporter: Oh I understand how that can be. Would you like to tell me about it?
Seeker: Ok. I have a friend who I've known a long time, who is one of my closest friends, but who is extremely insecure. She constantly seeks affirmation that I love and care for her, even though she should KNOW I do, since we have been friends for so long.
Supporter: I can understand how that can become a source of frustration after a while. Would you like to share what pushed it beyond the normal point today?
Seeker: It's just been an ongoing thing that has escalated recently because she's so afraid and timid and doesn't believe anyone could really love or care for her. I get sick of having to say that of course I love her.
Supporter: I can relate because I also have a close friend that seeks constant reaffirmations. Have you spoken with her about this?
Seeker: I have. I address it every time it comes up. She always sells herself short. Recently I suggested she could babysit my kids, she agreed, then almost immediately said it was ok if I had someone better in mind, and didn't want her, even though I had asked her! do you talk to your friend about it?
Supporter: Sometimes it is very difficult to see yourself through someone elses eyes when you undervalue yourself. I know it may be difficult to remain patient when your friend repeatedly does this, but maybe you could explain to her that it makes you feel like she is mistrustful of your opinion when she second guesses your taste in friends.
Seeker: Yes, I know. Until she finds her self worth, it doesn't matter what any of her friends say to her. I have actually told her that. That it seems like she doesn't trust me.
Supporter: Possibly explaining it in a way she can relate to would be helpful. I did in fact speak with my friend and it helped our relationship quite a bit. We continue to be very close 20 years later.
Seeker: It's frustrating to me and gives me anxiety because I wish I could change her to see herself the way I, and others, do. But I know I can't make her see her self worth. That's something she has to find for herself. That's good to hear about you and your friend.
Supporter: I can feel your frustration just by our conversation, and I too wish that she could see that you value both her and your friendship enough to reach out to someone that can just listen. Don't forget that your feelings are valid as well.
Seeker: I know they are. And yes, she's dealing with a lot, but we all are, and it would be so much better for her if she could trust the people who love her to actually love her.
Supporter: Sometimes you have to take a step back and fill your own cup.
Seeker: Indeed. Thank you for your input.
Supporter: Do you think a break would help you feel better able to deal with the demands of her friendship? Do you think a break would help you feel better able to deal with the demands of her friendship? It has been my pleasure! I trust you will make the right choice! Best of wishes!
Seeker: Not really, because I'd just worry about her. She needs someone like me to look after her. I'm kind of the Yin to her Yang. Thank you for your time and conversation!

Supporter: Hello there, how is life treating you at the moment?
Seeker: Not too bad outside of work. I'm miserable there.
Supporter: So you are experiencing problems at work? Please tell me about it, I am happy to listen.
Seeker: Things have changed and my new supervisor has crushed my spirit by taking all the parts I love away. She never liked me and now she gets to make me suffer.
Supporter: I am very sorry to hear that - trouble with workmates, especially those who are in a higher position, can make things very miserable can't they?
Seeker: They really can. I used to love my job and my team. Now she has made everyone miserable because she just doesn't care about learning the job or the job at all. My morale is low and worse because I can't help my peers who are struggling as well.
Supporter: Have you considered going over her head and putting in a complaint? Especially if she is making everyone else miserable as well. Someone more senior might be able to do something.
Seeker: I have considered this many times. Unfortunately, the next level manager doesn't respect or value my team in general. She has made that clear. She's also just awful and uncomfortable to talk to. I've found her to just be mean sometimes. It just feels so hopeless. Just waiting for someone to notice. Just hoping she fails. It's just really hard to show up everyday. But I do. Although the days are long and exhausting with no motivation to perform.
Supporter: Please try to stay positive - bullies never prosper in the long term. I think that you need to talk to your co-workers about this and see if you can come to some sort of arrangement between you Alternatively, have you ever considered seeking another job? I know that that might feel like selling out but you might be happier somewhere else
Seeker: You are right. She is a bully. I have called her several names to myself, but not a bully yet. My coworkers and I have discussed what options we may have. My suggestion was that we work at our normal pace rather than scrambling to make up for her failures. I wouldn't want to set her up, but I think her failing is the only way we will ever see a solution. I have applied for another job within my company. There seems to be interest in me, so that's exciting. It is a job I really want. But then, of course, I feel bad about leaving my peers behind. I really care about them.
Supporter: I feel that that is fair enough. You should not be working to make up for her failures and I hear you saying that you feel that this is w hat is happening?
Seeker: Definitely. Everyone is struggling. I am the one my team expects to help with some of the tasks she is not performing. I'm happy to do it for my team, but there is no recognition. But I think I have been giving them good advice about hanging in there, staying positive, etc... I should probably listen to myself.
Supporter: (sorry was afk give me a second to catch up :)) I really feel that you have grounds for a formal complaint. Just her being incapable is bad enough but bullying too is unacceptable
Seeker: You may be right. My company has an anonymous reporting system. I should learn a little more about how that works and see if that's an option. I'm not sure things could get much worse at this point. This could be my last ditch effort. That's good advice and you saying it directly to me makes me think I should lean into it. I can't just spin my wheels in misery much longer.
Supporter: Anonymous reporting sounds like a good thing, as long as it's not being abused. This sounds like a very good time to use it though I hope I have been able to give you some good advice here!
Seeker: Most definitely. I feel more confident now about the anonymous reporting. I'll gather some notes from my peers to ensure I have a viable complaint. That's so helpful. Thank you.

Supporter: Hope all is well
Seeker: well, i'm losing my job in january so that is freaking me out
Supporter: I can understand your feelings but I am sure there is a way out
Seeker: I've not looked for a job in 20 years!
Supporter: I was also in same situation and can fully understand how you feel but trust me you will enjoy once you start looking for job
Seeker: I've got to do a new resume and then figure out how people even apply these days
Supporter: Trust me it is easy these days to update resume as many templates available online and applying for job is easy as well. Many online options are available and you get a quick response.
Seeker: I've tried to get in touch with the unemployment office but they do not answer phones lately.
Supporter: Need not to worry about it. You can use search engine and just type the job matching your profile and apply online. Trust me you will be surprised to see many options.
Seeker: Well it is freaking me out - I will not be able to pay my bills if I don't have a job.
Supporter: I was exactly in same situations and can fully understand but trying all your options to look for job is good - apply online, call friends or family and see if they have openings where they work, look work online if you get any temporary work which can enable you to pay bills till you find better job.
Seeker: I'm willing to do temp work, etc.. I just have to make enough $ to pay the main bills like mortgage, etc.. it makes me so afraid that I won't be able to do t hat
Supporter: I am sure you will be able to manage all this and it is just temporary feeling you have.
Seeker: 7 i'm very upset that we are even losing our jobs.
Supporter: No need to upset as it part of life. Call your best friend and discuss your feeling and I am sure you will feel good.
Seeker: She's just been through this looking for a job thing so she should have some great answers and places to help me maybe
Supporter: Excellent!! - I am sure she will have very good suggestion and will be great support for you. It is always good to talk to people you are close.
Seeker: that is true!
Supporter: You can always share and contact me if you need any help. I will be happy to help. Take care.
Seeker: ok thank you

Supporter: Hello there
Seeker: Hi
Supporter: How are things going?
Seeker: Not good. I'm depressed.
Supporter: Is there anything in particular that has been bothering you recently?
Seeker: I don't have enough money to buy my 5 kids X-mas gifts. Hello? Are you still here?
Supporter: I'm really sorry to hear that, but I'm sure your love for your kids can still shine through
Seeker: I do love my kids, but they are expecting some toys and stuff from Santa.
Supporter: Would it be possible to look at some more home made stuff for this year that will still be fun and meaningful?
Seeker: I cannot craft. If I made them something it would be so bad.
Supporter: I know it can be really hard to feel like you can't make anything worthwhile, but I'm sure theres something you could come up with that could still put a smile on your kids faces
Seeker: Do you have any craft ideas?
Supporter: Maybe you could look at involving your kids in the process. The feeling of doing something together as a family can make it way more fun. It could be a shared experience your family can look back on fondly later on.
Seeker: That's a good idea. I would like to have it done before christmas. How about some wooden toys or a cardboard box fort?
Supporter: I have seen some people make small ornaments filled with candies and treats and other small goodies. So even if all of the gifts feel small, they can feel like they are getting a lot of them. And you could even get them to have fun decorating and painting the ornaments! Yeah, a box fort is really fun!
Seeker: I never that about filling an ornament with small stuff. That's a great idea.
Supporter: When I was a kid, I loved making box forts, and its a great way to reuse stuff you might already have around the house. The fun pretend games you can play were a blast. I'm sure your kids might love it too!
Seeker: I could paint and decorate it. My daughters would like that. I can make it look like a castle.
Supporter: It can feel tough when it feels like you can't provide all the big gifts that you feel your kids deserve But you clearly care and love your kids, and want to do something for them
Seeker: I do. this has been very helpful. It's not all hopeless.
Supporter: Last Christmas when I gave gifts to my family, one of them later told me that the gift they loved the most was the box of Christmas cookies that they were able to enjoy over the course of the week afterwards, and not the keyboard I had gotten them. Sometimes it doesn't take something expensive to be meaningful and make someone happy
Seeker: That sounds wonderful. I'm getting to work on my projects. Thank you.

Seeker: Hello
Supporter: Hello, how are you doing today?
Seeker: I was looking for some assistance. I lost my job 4 month ago
Supporter: Losing your job is one of the biggest stressors in life, how have you been handling it?
Seeker: Well first few month was kind off alright, Was looking for a job in different places without success. And now I am really depressed and I feel so useless.
Supporter: I know what it's like to lose a job, and when it's hard to find a new one it can really make you feel low. What activities have you been doing in addition to seeking new employment?
Seeker: Nice that you understand me, I was trying job websites alongside with jobcenter in town centre. I have jobseeker allowance but it will not cover the rent
Supporter: I am living in a high-rent city and the only way I was able to keep my apartment was to find a roommate. Are there ways you can get help from friends or family until a new job opens up?
Seeker: I am renting just a room at the moment, Before I had a girlfriend so we had to split the bill. After she left I had to take all responsibility just on myself to pay bills. I have few friends but don't think they could lend me a lot of money anyway
Supporter: One possible solution, if it's possible for you, could be to sub-lease your room to someone else and stay with friends or family. Even if they can't loan you money, they may be able to let you stay with them for a week while you make money renting your room as an airbnb.
Seeker: Oh AirBnB might be a solution actually. I will speak to my cousin if I could stay couple of nights at his place.
Supporter: What sort of employment are you looking for? Perhaps we can brainstorm some places you can go to make connections for potential work.
Seeker: I was working in IKEA warehouse before I got redundant
Supporter: Working in a warehouse shows you have great skills for several other types of jobs. Have you checked small independent-contractor sites like TaskRabbit or Lyft to make extra funds while you search for a new permanent job?
Seeker: I even haven't heard about those. I am really useless sometimes... What kind of jobs I can find there do you know?
Supporter: Well, if you didn't know about them, that's not your fault. It's possible that you could find a new job opportunity while working on smaller tasks or by volunteering for a local organization. You could meet new folks who could provide you with new connections for employment!
Seeker: I Will definitely try that. You are really helpful. Have you been doing any jobs through those websites?
Supporter: Yes I am able to make a little spending money by doing small tasks like delivering real estate papers, or delivery take-out food. You can google a list of sites like RentSons.com where you can sign up to do an assortment of tasks, and your warehouse skills will come in handy!
Seeker: That's cool, I feel now a lot better. Maybe I will be able to find even a girlfriend somewhere on those jobs. I feel lonely after my girlfriend left me
Supporter: We all feel lonely when life gets hard, but getting yourself out there to do tasks will help you feel useful AND you could meet your future wife, you never know! I wish you the absolute best!
Seeker: Thank you very much for you help. I learned something new today and feel much better
Supporter: You're welcome. I think you'll do great.
Seeker: Have a lovely afternoon!

Seeker: Hello, I'm feeling a lot of anxiety.
Supporter: I am sorry to hear that. Do you know what may be causing ytour anxiety?
Seeker: I found out I'm losing my job on January 1.
Supporter: You lost your job? thats a tough situation. Is it due to covid?
Seeker: No, not due to covid. It's a gig job, much like mturk, but the company is dropping people from my state on that date.
Supporter: I know its tough especially with the holidays and all. You have so many great skills and are such a hard worker I dont think you will have a problem at all finding something different.
Seeker: I've been looking at other companies, but learning a new system after all these years is difficult.
Supporter: I remember a time I lost my job and felt my whole world crumbling but then I realized when one door closes another door opens. when those doors close it seems that its usually for the best because it opens the path for something bigger and greater for you.
Seeker: That's true. I've thought about looking into new fields.
Supporter: Have you looked into some evening classes or maybe online schooling? I hear there are so many different options when it comes to online learning.
Seeker: I was looking into that last night, but with covid, classes have had to cut enrollment and are already full for next semester.
Supporter: They are full? well what about surrounding towns? Have you sat down and really thought about your passions and what you enjoy doing? Maybe theres an elderly person who needs some companionship or something like that in town for the time being.
Seeker: I don't have a car, so I'm stuck doing classes locally. I think I'll just have to wait for the next semester.
Supporter: Is waiting until next semester something your willing to do? That would give you time to reflect on yourself and your future and figure out what you want to do as a career. I could give you a list of other online opportunities to make money if you would be interested.
Seeker: I would be interested in that, thank you.

Seeker: hello
Supporter: Hello. How are you today?
Seeker: not very good.
Supporter: oh no. that isn't good. can you tell me what happened?
Seeker: my husband and i have been fighting alot recently over his infidelity its really taken a toll on me. we have tried several counselors but nothing seems to be working
Supporter: I am sorry to hear that. I can understand how frustrating that can be. I have had my fair share of boyfriends cheat on me.
Seeker: weve been married for 14 years. I feel broken by this. we have 2 kids and my daughter, the eldest knows
Supporter: I am sure that you have been trying to do everything that you can do to help the situation. It sounds like you choosing counseling was a good start. It shows how much you care.
Seeker: yes but my husband doesnt want to fi things. hes happy with having 2 women ive had to buy a recorder and put it in his car. The things i heard were horrible. he found out though.
Supporter: It is rough for our children to see adult stuff like this. They might not be able to understand. I would suggest trying to set down and talk to them about it, when you are ready.
Seeker: I dont want my youngest to know. He loves his father and i dont want to destroy that
Supporter: How do you feel about your husband not wanting to fix things? Is that something that you are considering?
Seeker: i feel horrible. Im actually trying to fix things while he texts her every day i dont know whats gonna happen
Supporter: That is a very thoughtful thing for you to put your son first. He is lucky to have such a great mother, that obviously loves him.
Seeker: i do very much
Supporter: Have you tried to talk to your husband about your feelings and how you might not be willing to accept this?
Seeker: i do but every time i do he thinks that its that i dont trust him and that i hate him and i dont hate him or his lover. I just want things to go back they used to be. what should i do?
Supporter: Have you thought about if you can trust him after that?
Seeker: im not sure if i can, but i dont want to live in constant paranoia of him im just so lost
Supporter: I can understand where you are coming from. I have been in that situation myself and it is not an easy place to be. For me, it took some time to accept that I deserved better than someone who didn't just want me. Is that how you feel?
Seeker: kind of
Supporter: Understandably so. I believe that this is just temporary and you will be amazed at how strong you are.
Seeker: you think so?
Supporter: If you are leaning toward not accepting not being enough for him, then I would suggest an exit plan. Call a family member, or friend, to see if you can stay there awhile. Have a cooling off period from your husband and reassess the situation
Seeker: ok. ill consider that thank you so much this has been going on for half a year
Supporter: I absolutely do. We normally find out that we are actually much stronger than we give ourselves credit for.
Seeker: thank you
Supporter: That is wonderful news! See you are starting to make a plan for a better life for you and your children. You so got this!
Seeker: thank you so much. stay safe bye bye
Supporter: youre welcome. I am here if you need me
Seeker: i have a feeling that everything will be okay.
Supporter: That is great! Did you have a chance to think of anything else that might help you through this?
Seeker: yes. Thanks to you i can broaden my search thank you. good bye

Seeker: I am so embarassed and saddened. I can not believe he cheated on me. I thought we were going to work out. I was really attracted into him and I cared for him a lot. I wanted to date him longer. Thank Goodness I did not sleep with him. What a disaster. Why are men like this? Why do they break women's hearts? I wish there were more decent men out there that did not play around. Men can be such pigs!
Supporter: what happened?
Seeker: I met a handsome intelligent man.
Supporter: how are you feeling lately?
Seeker: We dated for a month. Then out of nowhere he cheated on me. I'm so sad. I am just trying to understand what I did wrong.
Supporter: it's okay. we should learn from things like this.
Seeker: That's true. It's crazy we have to experience heart ache. To learn...
Supporter: don't think much and keep yourself engaged in the activities you like the most.
Seeker: Hey, that is great advice!
Supporter: can you tell me how are you before this incident?
Seeker: I was happy. But when a man breaks your heart, it makes you feel very ugly.
Supporter: can you share me some happy memories which made you smile can you share me some happy memories which made you smile
Seeker: Sure, I love going to the movies! How about you!
Supporter: it's okay. i can understand. yeah me too. i love movies and traveling.
Seeker: Are you American?
Supporter: I love traveling to new places.
Seeker: Yes traveling is what we are made to do as humans!
Supporter: yes, i am an american.what about you
Seeker: Same
Supporter: well, just think of some happy memories and try to spend time with people who value you the most.
Seeker: Yes, thank you for the great advice! Like Thanksgiving, I hope you have wonderful memories with your friends and family next week.
Supporter: oh, thats nice of you.thank you
Seeker: You are very welcomed!
Supporter: you too!
Seeker: Well what are you having for lunch?
Supporter: i had my breakfast just now. i am planning to cook some beef for lunch.what about you
Seeker: Spicy pork tamales.. I like that not thinking about my break up makes me happy. Like talking to you about whatever else.

Seeker: hello
Supporter: Hi how are you ?
Seeker: Well im feeling awful and my heart is racing , im feeling anxious for no reason.
Supporter: I understand what your going thru , i also suffered from anxiety but trust we you will overcome this.
Seeker: What do you recommend i do?
Supporter: I recommend searching online about meditation , also one of thing that helped the most for me was exercise and eating healthy.
Seeker: Ive tried meditation but cant seem to calm down. Exercise help for a bit but then my anxiety comes back.
Supporter: I remember many times i thought the same way as you but i didnt give up and kept trying. As long as you dont give up you will make progress. It will take time and patience.
Seeker: Wow its so nice to talk to someone who had the same issues. Are there any other suggestions you might recommendo?
Supporter: OF course , for example i watched youtube videos of someone called theanxietyguy and i made tremendous progress with him. Also i drink teas to calm my nerves .
Seeker: Thank you!! im going to look him up . Has your anxiety come back?
Supporter: Somethings its want to come back but i am on top of it and always being discipline with myself. I make sure to love myself first and give myself priority.
Seeker: Thank you for everything .I am now motivated to get going.
Supporter: You are welcomed i am glad i was able to help out. Stay positive and healthy.
Seeker: What kind of teas do you drink to help with anxiety?
Supporter: I drink a lot of chamomile tea with honey which has a great flavor good to calm done, i drink mint tea very refreshing and tilo tea which helps me sleep.
Seeker: I never tried tea , this new for me . I will definitely order some online. DO you have any other suggestions?
Supporter: Yes of course. If you worried about some kind of sickness i would recommend you go to the doctor get yourself a full checkup it will help calm you mind down and reassure you that you are healthy.
Seeker: That a greay idea. My health anxiety its at all high levels everything i see about a sickness i get worry especially with this covid -19. I barely go out and get nervous. Has that happened to you?
Supporter: Yes, once in while i get nervous about but i try to keep positive and take the right precautions and wear my mask, clea my hands and stay my distance. you shouldnt have a issues . Do you workout?
Seeker: No, i havent felt motivated . What kind of workout do you recommend for my anxiety?

Supporter: Hello, how are you doing today?
Seeker: I am feeling angry today about work.
Supporter: Oh no, what happened to make you feel this way?
Seeker: My coworker expects me to do things the way she does and is constantly critical. I just want her to understand that I am able to do things my way and it is still okay. I told her this and she ignored me.
Supporter: I'm sure that's terribly frustrating having someone treat you like that. Is this something that your boss is aware of?
Seeker: I have not told her yet. I do not want to get her into trouble and I want to have a good relationship with her.
Supporter: Can you discuss it with her in a respectful way to get her to understand that you're not trying to undermine her but that this is how you work most efficiently? And maybe mention that you don't want to involve the boss?
Seeker: That's something I could try. I really care about my coworker and it makes me so angry that she treats me this way.
Supporter: I think sometimes it's easy to jump to anger when you feel hurt. It might be worth telling her how you feel and also maybe ask why she thinks you should be doing things her way. Maybe there's a give and take in this situation. Some of her methods could be beneficial.
Seeker: Do you have any advice on how to start my conversation with her? I have found some of her ideas to be beneficial. I just would like my ideas expressed as well. I feel we can learn from each other.
Supporter: Tell her the things that you like about her method and maybe suggest some of your methods to her as well. Maybe she'll find them to be more efficient. Make it a partnership rather than a fight for whose method is better. She could feel threatened by you so it's worth digging into those feelings with her and proving to her that you're working toward the same goal.
Seeker: That's a great idea. It is possible. I am the new kid on the block. I will try by being non confrontational. Any specific ideas to how I can do that? She gets offended easily. I want her to know I am helping.
Supporter: I'd suggest how much she's helped you since you are in fact the new kid on the block. And tell her that you want to work with her to have the most efficient partnership possible and use each of your talents to the best of your ability. Then you can lay out how you work best and see where it goes from there.
Seeker: Thanks! I will try that. You made me feel so much better!
Supporter: I'm so glad, these can be frustrating situations but sometimes it's worth looking at the other person's perspective.
Seeker: I agree. Sometimes you just have to take a step back and have a conversation with someone not in the thick of it.
Supporter: Absolutely, I have no emotional stake in this. The two of you do and that can cloud things sometimes.
Seeker: I think people get territorial when they have worked somewhere and a new person comes in. I see that now. I am optimistic we will work it out and be a great team!
Supporter: That's great to hear, I'm glad we were able to chat!
Seeker: Me too! You really helped me. Have a wonderful day! I know I will since you helped me out.

Supporter: Hi! What kind of issue are you dealing with today? I would love to help :)
Seeker: I am still depressed about losing my job.
Supporter: Oh no! I'm so sorry to hear that. What have you been doing since losing your job?
Seeker: It's been rough, it was out of the clear blue. I've been looking for a job, then the pandemic hit.
Supporter: Oh wow I feel you. I have loved ones that have gone through the same thing as you. They were starting to feel super down about themselves. I tried my best to support and encourage them not to give up.
Seeker: Yea, I know, it's not just me. But I do feel alone. I know how they feel.
Supporter: What industry do you work in? With the pandemic, a lot of interviews are done through Zoom and of course not everyone is at the best through video
